original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: Precompute immutable additive and unit inverse tables in the complete PR6210 command, prove scoped equivalence, and measure unchanged complete replays.
scope_change_reason: Select one complete radical-fanout replay and preserve its entire finite workload. This is verifier engineering, not a new tariff or an audit.
bottleneck_link: Remove repeated finite-ring inverse scans without dropping checks, so complete mechanism replays require less interpreter work.
stop_rule: Ship the first exact work reduction with unchanged complete output. Do not extend the mathematical tariff or optimize other paths.
evidence: Full-command tuple.index count decreases from 1661695 to 260; all complete stdout is identical. 322 index cases and 16 controls pass. Ten alternating full-command pairs have zero errors; wall-time comparison remains inconclusive because timing ranges overlap.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Does the unchanged complete command show a stable wall-time gain on an idle Linux CPython 3.12 host?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact repeated-search reduction is portable; elapsed-time gains depend on the host and remaining interpreter work.
open_questions.first_step: Run benchmark.py for at least five alternating pairs, preserving all output digests, and report medians and ranges.
open_questions.blocked_by: An additional host measurement; no missing executable dependency.
